notes.title: Major Update - Early Access Build 4
notes.notes:
Hey there,

The new early access build is here! After the early access launch back in March, I took a step back to process all the feedback and take some time to rethink the core of Hexagod based on your feedback. Although I think the game was fun, it has some major flaws that I wanted to address, while keeping the fun of tile placement and exploiting adjacency bonuses to gain massive amounts of resources.

So I did just that! 

[h2]Summary of Changes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] I removed Wonders as a win condition, and instead you now need to reach a Quota each day and simply put you gain quota by collecting resources. If you run out of turns on day without reaching the quota you lose. Survive for 3 weeks and you win. I think this system leans more into the fantasy of creating a thriving village. My goal is to then reward you for careful tile placement and strategic exploitation of adjacency effects via this Quota system. 
[*] Villagers are now called Workers and they are tied to a Village and will work the tile they are on at the end of turn. Workers can only be assigned to adjacent tiles and only one Worker per tile.
[*] You Villagers (now called Workers) no longer die if they are not fed each day, instead now your villages will consume food each turn to grow. After they consume enough food they will grow a new worker. Each turn they can eat food equal to their number of workers.
[*] All tile improvements and tile based resources are permanent. This means as you place things your village will be growing in power. This will hopefully remove the tedious nature of needing to replace those Berry Bushes.
[*] The Tech Tree has been removed and instead each day you get a set of cards and tile groups to purchase with resources. At the end of the day you earn coins which you can spend in the shop to buy cards, relics, and new villages.
[/list]

This is just the beginning of my ideas for tile improvements, buildings, and relics. 

In the coming patches I want to add:
[list]
[*] Consumables (change tile type, add +1 worker to a village, remove an improvement, etc.) My plan is for you to find these on discoverable islands as well as be able to purchase them in the Shop
[*] Packs (example: Food Pack which would give you a choice of 3 food based cards). This would be part of the Shop
[*] Other ideas you have?
[/list]

I already know the balance of the game is a bit off, so please try and break my game and then post about. Bonus points if you can break the UI with how large your numbers get!

Cheers,
Aarimous

notes.title: Tile Improvements Rework Again, Corruption System, Bug Fixes and QoL
notes.notes:
Hello there,

This patch contains a big change to how you get tile improvements and a new tile corruption system. I have removed the rotating shop and instead at the end of each day you will select a new tile improvement to be able to build. My goal with this change is to lean into the roguelike nature of the game, but remove the annoyance that a rotating shop brought. 

I have also added a new system I'm calling the corrupted tile system. At Day 20 a corrupted origin tile will spawn adjacent to a random tile. Then at the end of each day the corruption will spread to tiles that are adjacent to corrupted tiles. When a tile is corrupted any resource or buildings will be destroyed and if a villager is left on a tile it will die at the end of a turn. It will also start to spread more and more each day (1 tile the first day, 2 the next, 3, and so on). 

I will add a setting to turn this off for players who want a more chill run, but while having people playtest Hexagod I realized there is a lot of fun and replayability to trying to win the game as quickly as possible. This system is aimed at pushing the player to play fast and really min/max each run. This is the first pass at this system so I will need to adjust the balance or tone down some of the mechanics here. Plus I need to add some more polish.

I believe this patch will be the final feature that I add before the February Next Fest. In the coming weeks I will start to add more tile improvements, relics, art, and generally polish as much as I can.

Cheers,
Aarimous

The card/pack system was ultimately uninteresting and frankly annoying. As such I have killed it and added the ability to directly purchase the improvements you want from the shop. I think the new system will allow me to focus in on the core fun of placing tiles to min/max your adjacency bonuses.  

This patch also comes with a lot of small changes to improve clarity and or remove unnecessary mechanic like victory points. My goal right now is to release weekly patches, so check back soon for more sweeping overhauls and reworks.

Cheers,
Aarimous

notes.title: The Great Tile Placement Update - Demo 0.6.0
notes.notes:
Hello there,

This patch is part one of a three part plan to do a mini-rework of Hexagod. Over the past month I have been trying to make combat in Hexagod fun and interesting (while not being too complicated), and ultimately it wasn't working. This is because at its core I want Hexagod to be a fun peaceful village builder with a little bit of strategy. Combat ran counter to those goals and as such I have disabled it in the game. 

Instead I want to address some of the large issues in the game first of which is tile placement. In it's previous state tile placement was more or less cosmetic only and this rework is centered around making tile placement feel interesting and meaningful. 

The first phase of this is moving tile placement out of packs and cards and into the shop. You'll now be able to place groups of 4 random tiles (smart randomness coming soon). As you are placing the group you can rotate clockwise/counterclockwise. This single change has made tile placement far more fun and has really opened the design space up.

Here is a devlog chatting about this patch and my goals for combat:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VmMrS_q7-fw

In the next two phases I plan on adding in mechanical benefits which will further reward smart tile placement.

Phase 2: adjacency bonuses and tile resources
Phase 3: resource expansion

Please let me know if you have any ideas or questions. I always knew combat might ruin the game, but I needed to explore that idea fully and ultimately I think my gut was correct.

Cheers,
Aarimous


[h2]Demo 0.6.0 Patch Notes:[/h2]
[h3]Reworked Tile Placement[/h3]
[list]
[*] Goal: make tile placement more interesting and and open up the design space for tile adjacency bonuses
[*] Now you will buy and place groups of tiles directly from the shop
[*] Select the tile group by left clicking and cancel the selection by right clicking
[*] You can rotate the tile group by using the UI button in the shop or by pressing Q/E for clockwise/counter-clockwise rotation respectively
[*] You get a free daily reroll
[*] The cost will scale up each time you buy a tile group
[/list]

[h3]Combat and Unit Stats[/h3]
[list]
[*] Combat and evil hexes have been disabled (likely forever)
[*] Simply put this system was changing the core vibes of this game, and although combat could be fun it just didn't fit for my vision of Hexagod
[/list]
  
[h3]Other Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Changed the cost and values of almost all the buildings (this will change)
[*] Fast forward now is 4x instead of 3x (just seeing how this feels)
[*] Increased the tile victory points
[*] Adjusted the card artwork for clarity (will likely change this again)
[*] Move the bottom bar to the top
[*] Removed military resources (for now)
[*] Added in icons for the various screens
[*] Moved favor to the resource bar and added in a shop button
[*] Adjusted the first quest to now reference tile groups
[*] Probably a bunch of bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Update 0.5.0
notes.notes:
Hello there,

In this patch you’ll find a large rework of the evil hex system, the addition of demons, and a new combat system. In my head this is only version 1 of combat. I have a long list of things I still need to add, but I wanted to release this patch now so I can fix any bugs in the core of combat and get feedback from you on the UI and UX for combat.

Here is a devolg chatting about this patch and my goals for combat:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FzDXm3F9pN0

In the next patch my plan is to add in items which you’ll be able to equip to your villagers. My goal for items is to allow you to specialize your villagers into combat, support, or resource gathering. More to come soon.

Please let me know if you have any ideas or questions. In my head combat is going to be the system which will take Hexagod from a good game to a great game.. or it could ruin the fun entirely, but let’s not let that happen.

Cheers,
Aarimous

notes.title: Demo Update 0.4.0
notes.notes:
Hey there,

The main thing this patch adds is the tile sub type system. Subtypes have been cooking in my head for a while and I am excited to get a working version into Hexagod. 

The main goal with this system is to make tile placement more interesting. You will now be rewarded for planning out tile placements which result in sub types since the bonus effects are designed to be a bit OP. The other goal is to give you a sense of discovery and AHA moments when you find a new subtype or take advantage of a bonus effect.

My next goal will be to work on a major rework of villagers and evil hexes. 

More to come!
Aarimous


[h2]Demo 0.4.0 Patch Notes:[/h2]
[h3]Added Tile Subtypes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Tile subtypes are enhanced versions of base tiles that provide powerful bonus effects while retaining the base type's original properties.
[*] A tile automatically transforms into a subtype once its corresponding recipe is completed.
[*] To complete a recipe, you need a central tile surrounded by 6 adjacent tiles.
[*] Most recipes require a combination of 2 tile types: the central tile must be one of these types, and the surrounding 6 tiles must consist of exactly 3 of each type.
[*] There are 15 recipes which covers all pairing of the 6 placeable tile base types
[*] Alternatively, some recipes require the central tile to be surrounded entirely by matching tile types.
[*] There are 6 recipes like this (one for each placeable base type)
[/list]

[h3]Secrets Screen[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a new button in the bottom right to show the discovered secrets.
[*] This popup will be expanded to show more info about things you have found like cards, evil hexes, etc..
[*] Discovering a subtype will unlock the recipe in this screen so you can reference is later
[/list]
    
[h3]Other Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated the tile tooltip to improve readability and gave it a smoother animation for when it shows/hides
[*] Added some UI to show the controls. This is shown at during the “End of Day” phase and when you open the options menu. I also added these to the HELP popup
[*] Added in a bunch of new cards
[*] Rebalanced a lot of the cards
[*] Changed which cards are in which pack
[*] Adjusted some the text in the quests
[*] UI elements will now slowly fade in as the info they show becomes relevant
[*] Updated various artwork for icons to have more consistent visual
[*] Added new icons in various places
[*] Added new sound effects and adjusted volume levels for others
[*] Added in a small save file which will save your audio settings
[*] Added in a player progression save file which will save info about which Sub Type Recipes you have discovered
[*] Added text to show the current demo build
[*] Updated the font for parts of the UI to use version of the font which looks better at smaller font sizes (Help text, quest text, etc..)
[*] Bug fixes (probably a lot that I can’t recall at this point)
[/list]
